# maak

> maak is a command runner whose task file is a Guile Scheme module: every
> procedure in `maak.scm` is a task, its docstring is its documentation, and a
> command is an argv list rather than a shell string. There is no DSL — the build
> is the program. MIT licensed, POSIX and Guile, no Windows.

A task is read as code, so a description of a project's automation is never
guessed from output. The two objects to read instead are `maak --list --json`
(the tasks of the current file: docstring, line, dependencies, example,
arguments) and `maak --plan --json TASK` (what a task would execute: `kind`,
`argv`, `cwd`, `env`, `elevation`, `devNull`, `async`), both versioned.

## Start here

- [Quick start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/quick-start.org): your first Maak file, eight steps from a module to a dry run.
- [Tasks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/tasks.org): how a procedure becomes a task, what `#:export` hides, how arguments arrive, how `--list` lays docstrings out.
- [The command line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/cli.org): every option, the grammar of tasks and arguments, environment files, load paths.
- [The built-in toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/builtins.org): `run`, pipelines, background jobs, file helpers, `task-error`, string helpers, gettext.
- [Plans, watches and explanations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/inspect.org): the typed plan behind `--plan`, its two JSON shapes, and what `explain` reports.
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/configuration.org): the `MAAK_*` environment variables and the Scheme parameters behind dry-run and quiet.

## For an assistant

- [Maak files and AI assistants](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/ai.org): what to ask maak instead of guessing, the rules a Maak file is reviewed against, the traps a first draft falls into, and a block to paste into a project's `AGENTS.md`.
- [The skill file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/contrib/ai/maak-skill.md): one Markdown file to add to a context — module header, rules, vocabulary, Guile forms, verification loop.
- [Why maak, and why Lisp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/why-maak.org): what Make cannot express, and the table of Make flags that carried over.
- [What 1.0 freezes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/stability.org): which of those shapes are promises to a consumer, and how a deprecation travels.
- [Task files in JSON, TOML and YAML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/task-files.org): a task list without the language, and what a data file cannot do.

## The rest of the guide

- [Guide index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/index.org): one page per topic — Guix and Nix, containers, Rust, Python, frontend, Maven and Gradle, Emacs Lisp, git and archives, downloads, editors.
- [This repository's own automation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/project.org): the tasks of the checkout that writes maak.
- [Hacking on maak](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjba23/maak/trunk/docs/development.org): the Veritas suite, the API documentation, the man page.
